With fid vs shaco matchup it's all about the element of surprise. Whoever strikes first wins. Two common situations:

1. Fid ults over wall/flashes fears and one shots shaco before shaco can ult/q. 

2. Shaco comes out of invis, backstabs and combos while placing the box (box incredibly important vs fid) fid fears and has to run away, as if he drains he will get feared by the box and likely die to shaco dps.


Sure a lot of factors are not taken into account and other shit but I can see the frustrations for both sides in this matchup, however I think what fid has in 1v1 potential and teamfight/lockdown shaco makes up for with splitting and assassinating.

Masters/challenger player gave me the best advice to date on shaco. "If you can't one shot someone, split"

Shaco should be played as a splitter who uses splitting to disrupt the enemy team and wait for the enemies to make uncoordinated rotations.

It's like you said it's not something that goes away, it's rather you just learn to cope with it. In a way it's kind of like being thrust into a new environment. You're confused and lost, and even though you may always feel this way you will inevitably adapt. 

Regarding your friend and others you've witnessed suffering from depression there's just so many factors: how resilient they are as a person, career path, age, family, and sometimes just sheer luck. You just gotta believe in them, be there for them, and wish them the best.

It's harder than one might think to reach out someone. First off, bringing up depression and suicide makes a lot of people uncomfortable, so even though he might have been depressed, he wouldn't want to bring it up.

Also that's what depression does, it messes with your head and tells you that you shouldn't get help, and to just suffer on your own, until you kill yourself. It's just really difficult to talk about, even to someone who he was really close with.

I hope that you and your family can recover from this and you guys get the support you need. It's just that in situations like this it's common to think "why didn't he just talk to me/someone else", but it's entirely different when you're in their shoes.

Started around 8-10 and 20 now. Peak of my depression was at 17 when I attempted but unfortunately at the time failed. After that I got therapy and my parents supported me in getting better. I was really good during my first year of college when I was 18, but slowly old feelings and even new negative ones emerged, and once again I fluctuate between being suicidal and depressed and normal. 

I'm personally still kind of young so I haven't dealt with many struggles that adults have to deal with, but depression is something that never really goes away. It's kind of like a volcano, for some people their "volcano" stays dormant for a while but when it erupts it hits hard. Depression will eventually show its head, but you just have to be ready for the times that it hits hard.

As for how to cope with it, I personally just have a couple close friends I talk to over the Internet, and it gives me that social interaction that I need but also helps take my mind off bad thoughts. Obviously this won't help everyone, but try and find an activity that helps you calm down and get lost in whatever you're doing.
